supports: The Python package is bindings over the Rust implementation. The speed line on that page is not on a slide. The caption quotes one sentence from this page.
The repo is Rust (Cargo.toml and src/lib.rs, with a PyO3 import under the python feature). The slide says tiktoken is the OpenAI tokenizer in Rust. The README speed line is not on a slide.

From V2, validation and serialization live in pydantic-core, which is Rust. Model definition stays in pydantic. The page that loaded from the docs.pydantic.dev architecture URL. The 5 to 20 multiplier is not on a slide.
Polars is a DataFrame query engine written in Rust, with a Python API. The slide says Polars runs table queries in Rust.

PDS-H scale factor 10 totals: pandas 2.2.3 at 365.71 seconds, polars streaming 1.30.0 at 3.89 seconds, printed factor 94.0. Machine: AWS c7a.24xlarge, 96 vCPUs and 192 GB. Pandas was not run at scale factor 100. Not re-run here.
Ruff is a Python linter and formatter written in Rust. The 10-100x line and the chart are not on a slide.
uv is a Python package and project manager written in Rust. The 10-100x line is not on a slide.
Rust has no garbage collector. The type system and ownership model check memory safety at compile time. The homepage wording blazingly fast is not on a slide.

Louis Imershein, 15 Sep 2025. In the default build the GIL blocks CPU-bound threads. Threads overlap on an I/O wait. He writes that a CUDA call releases the GIL. The path he describes is profile, then a PyO3 extension. His timings are not on a slide.
NumPy element-by-element array math runs as pre-compiled C code. The slide does not say NumPy has no Fortran, and it does not say NumPy moved to Rust.
The PyTorch C++ frontend is a C++ library for CPU and GPU tensor computation.
torch.cuda runs CUDA operations. The slide line is that PyTorch tensor code is C++ and CUDA.
PyTorch is a Python package for tensor computation with GPU acceleration. The README says it is not a Python binding into a monolithic C++ framework. The slide does not call PyTorch a thin wrapper.
Qdrant is written in Rust. A Python client calls it. Latency and size claims on the repo are not on a slide.
Lance and LanceDB are written in Rust, with a Python client. Marketing figures on the FAQ are not on a slide.
Candle is a minimalist ML framework for Rust. The slide calls it an optional runtime that does not replace PyTorch.
Burn is a tensor library and a deep learning framework in Rust. The README version discussion is not on a slide. The slide says Burn does not replace PyTorch.
The free-threaded build is supported in Python 3.14 and is still optional. It is not the default. The single-thread penalty percentage is not on a slide.
PEP 779 is Final for Python 3.14. Phase II: the free-threaded build is officially supported and still optional. Phase III, making it the default, is a later decision.
The default build is the GIL-enabled build. The free-threaded build is separate. The slide does not name the python3.14t binary.
PyO3 is Rust bindings for Python, including native extension modules. Guide banner v0.29.3 on this date. The last slide names PyO3 for a profiled CPU path.
